newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank raises overnight rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank raises overnight rates.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Thursday it raised its overnight rates by two percentage points each.
Its closely-watched overnight borrowing rate now stands at 32 percent, while its lending rate was set 34 percent.
This fourth increase by the Central Bank in more than a week brought the total increase to 17 percentage points since last week's de facto devaluation of the Thai baht.
The Central Bank had to raise rates again in the wake of Wednesday's renewed speculation brought on by a newspaper report the Monetary Board would discuss the devaluation of the peso on Wednesday.
The report by Singapore Strait Times was denied by government officials.
Traders estimated the Central Bank may have unloaded about $645 million to calm the market on Wednesday.
The latest 32 percent overnight borrowing rate exceeds the 30 percent-high in March 1995 when the Central Bank also had to defend the peso in the aftermath of the Mexican peso crisis.
